Hi Alex / Sam 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps we discussed: 

What we heard from ACME:
- Primary goal: accurate, grounded responses for customer-facing knowledge base search (chat + answer pages).
- Volume: ~2M monthly queries; 10-15% peak concurrency.
- SLAs: target p95 latency < 600ms for short queries, strong grounding (>95% cite accuracy).
- Constraints: some PII in documents, must support VPC + audit logs.

Redwood recommendations (high-level):
1) Retrieval settings: dense faiss index with hybrid BM25 fallback; initial chunk size 500 tokens; top_k_retriever=50, top_k_reranker=10.
2) Reranker: use lightweight cross-encoder reranker fine-tuned on your domain (we prototyped with redwood-cross-3.7b-rr).
3) Model candidates for generation: redwood-instruct-13b-quant for baseline; redwood-xlarge-33b for higher-fidelity where cost allows.
4) Prompt + grounding: explicit system instructions, citations template, and a short provenance post-process to surface source links.

Deliverables we agreed on:
- Share the evaluation artifacts: prompt sets, reranker benchmarks, and overall summary report (attached).
- Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) to run a 2-week pilot: data ingest -> index creation -> eval on your holdout prompts -> review.
- Technical kickoff w/ Dylan + infra team next Thursday (Aug 6) to finalize indexing and VPC details.

Attached: acme_rag_eval_summary.pdf (high-level results), prompt_set_v1.json (holdout+probe prompts), reranker_benchmarks.csv (proto numbers).

Next steps for Alex / ACME:
- Confirm availability for kickoff on Aug 6 (30-45 min).
- Share the sample export for indexing (S3 link or Drive).
- Any compliance constraints we should pre-load for the pilot (retention windows, redaction rules).

I'll loop Dylan in for technical details below. Thanks  excited to get this going.

Hey all  quick technical notes ahead of the kickoff. Marissa covered most of it, but a few specifics to help Alex's compliance and latency questions: 

Reranker latency & ops:
- Cross-encoder (3.7B prototype) avg latency: ~45-70ms per pair on a T4-class GPU / ~18-30ms on A100/RTX6000-ish. With top_k_reranker=10 and batch scoring you can expect ~200-400ms of extra latency on A100 for the reranker stage. If p95 budget is under 600ms, that leaves ~200-300ms for generation and routing - workable with redwood-instruct-13b-quant if generation lengths are short (~40-80 tokens).
- If latency still tight, we can run a two-stage approach: bi-encoder shortlist (fast, CPU-friendly) -> small cross-encoder re-rank on a subset (top_k=10) to reduce compute. That gives most quality gains with lower cost.

Retriever integration:
- Redwood can integrate with external vector stores (we've built connectors for Elastic, Pinecone, and S3-backed FAISS). For the pilot, keeping ACME's Elastic + a lightweight vector overlay is fine - we can index to a Faiss shard in Redwood Private and mirror updates via S3 snapshoting. This avoids full migration during pilot.

Audit logs / compliance:
- Redwood Private supports document access logs (document_id, timestamp, request_id, requester_identity). We can export logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or to an S3 bucket. We'll document retention windows per your legal team's requirements.

Experiment plan suggestion for the 2-week pilot (technical):
1) Ingest 100k doc subset -> build vector index (chunk=500)
2) Run retrieval-only baseline (top_k_retriever=50) -> measure recall@50 and grounding accuracy on your holdout prompts
3) Run bi-encoder + cross-encoder pipeline (reranker top10) and compare precision@10, generation grounding metrics, and end-to-end latency
4) If cross-encoder cost too high, test bi-encoder + light transformer re-ranker (smaller model) as fallback

I'll bring a short technical checklist to the kickoff to confirm infra (VPC endpoints, KMS, S3 access, network egress policy).
—Dylan
